chunks: Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a house that fell upon a group gathered together, and it was not known which of them died before the other. He said: “Some of them inherit from others.”

I said: “Abū Ḥanīfah introduced another view into it.” He said: “And what did he introduce into it?” I said: “He said that if two men, one of whom had one hundred thousand and the other had nothing, were in a ship and drowned, and it was not known which of them died first, then the inheritance would go to the heirs of the one who had nothing, and the heirs of the one who had wealth would receive nothing.”
So Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “He has indeed heard it, and it is like this.”

key_terms.الْمِيرَاثُ: the inherited estate or inheritance distribution
key_terms.بَيْتٍ وَقَعَ: a collapsed house causing a shared fatal incident
key_terms.سَفِينَةٍ: a ship, used here as an example of a shared accidental death
key_terms.وَرَثَةِ: the legal heirs of a deceased person
key_terms.يُوَرَّثُ بَعْضُهُمْ مِنْ بَعْضٍ: they inherit from one another in cases of uncertain order of death

ai.seo_question: What is the inheritance ruling when people die together and it is unknown who died first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on inheritance when multiple people die in a shared accident and the order of death is unknown. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that they inherit from one another, and he affirms the ruling when a comparable case involving drowning at sea is mentioned. The narration is significant in fiqh for cases of uncertain sequence of death affecting estate distribution.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5659 - Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abdur Rahman, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

I asked Imam (as) about a house that collapsed on a group of people gathered together, and it was not known who among them died first.
Imam (as) said: "They inherit from one another."

I said: "Abu Hanifah has given a different ruling regarding this."
Imam (as) asked: "And what did he say?"
I replied: "He said that if two men were on a ship, one of whom had one hundred thousand (in wealth) and the other had nothing, and the ship sank, and it was not known which of them died first, the inheritance would go to the heirs of the one who had nothing, and the heirs of the wealthy one would receive nothing."
Abu Abdullah (as) said: "Indeed, he has heard it, and it is exactly as it should be."
